ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Act on Reporting and Using of Specific Financial Transaction Information (Act No. 18953, effective Jan. 1, 2023), the Real Name Financial Transactions Act (Act No. 18912), the Commercial Act (Act No. 18959, Articles 289, 292, 317, 330), the Foreign Investment Promotion Act (Act No. 18865), and the Enforcement Decree of the Act on Reporting and Using of Specific Financial Transaction Information (Presidential Decree No. 33843), together with the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) Recommendations as implemented in Korea via the Financial Regulatory Reform Act.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation (Certified Extract of the Commercial Registry)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Commercial Registration Section of the Local District Court Registry Office in the Republic of Korea (e.g., Seoul Central District Court)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For use in a Hague Apostille Convention member state, obtain a certified copy of the registry extract from the court and then apply for an Apostille certificate from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea (Apostille Section). For use in a non-member state, the same certified copy must first be authenticated by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and then submitted for Consular Legalization at the embassy or consulate of the destination country in Seoul. These two routes are parallel; never chain Apostille with Consular Legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Certificate of No Tax Arrears)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National Tax Service of the Republic of Korea (issued through the Hometax system)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: A printed and sealed tax clearance certificate must be notarized by a Korean notary public (if requested by the receiving authority), then apostilled by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea for Apostille Convention member states. For non-member states, after notarization, the document is authenticated by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and then legalized by the consulate of the destination country in Seoul. The apostille route and the consular route are mutually exclusive alternatives.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney for Entity Formation and Registered Agent Appointment
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors of the corporate shareholder (or the ultimate beneficial owners) in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Execute the resolution/PoA before a notary public in the country of origin. If the country of origin is a party to the Hague Apostille Convention, attach an Apostille issued by the country's designated competent authority; the Korean registry accepts this without additional consular legalization. If the country of origin is not a member of the Apostille Convention, the document must be authenticated by the origin country's foreign ministry and then legalized by the Korean embassy or consulate in that country before it may be filed in Korea. No sequential combination of Apostille and Consular Legalization is permitted.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Incorporation (Charter) of the Chusik Hoesa
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Korean Notary Public (notarization is mandatory for stock company articles under Article 292 of the Korean Commercial Act)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: The notarized articles are filed with the local court registry. For overseas use, a certified copy of the notarized articles must be obtained from the notary public, then apostilled by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea for member states; for non-member states, the certified copy must be authenticated by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and then legalized at the destination country's consulate in Seoul. Use only one of these authentication pathways.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter for the Ultimate Beneficial Owner / Parent Company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: The financial institution maintaining the corporate or personal account of the shareholder/UBO (head office or designated branch)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: The bank letter must be signed by an authorized bank officer and notarized by a notary public in the bank's jurisdiction. If that jurisdiction is an Apostille Convention member, obtain an Apostille from the relevant national competent authority. If it is not a member, the notarized letter must be authenticated by the local foreign ministry and then legalized by the Korean consulate in that jurisdiction. This is an exclusive alternative to the Apostille route.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Before incorporation, the Korean registered agent and compliance counsel must screen all directors, shareholders holding at least 25% beneficial ownership, and any ultimate beneficial owners against the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List (SDN), the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and the Korean government's financial sanctions lists issued by the Ministry of Economy and Finance and the Financial Services Commission. For any politically exposed person (PEP), or person closely connected to a PEP, a high-risk customer classification requiring enhanced due diligence applies. The exact match or near match triggers a Suspicious Transaction Report to the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU) before proceeding. All screening must be documented and retained for a minimum of five years in accordance with the Financial Transaction Reports Act.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Internet Registration Office (IRO) of the Supreme Court of the Republic of Korea (https://www.iro.go.kr)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name must be written in Hangul (Korean script). A foreign-language name (such as English) may be additionally recorded as a trade name in the Articles of Incorporation, but the statutory registered name is the Hangul version. The four-tier naming convention requires: (a) a distinctive element (e.g., a brand or invented word), (b) an optional descriptive element of the business purpose, (c) the legal form suffix 'Chusik Hoesa' (stock corporation), and (d) the English equivalent 'Co., Ltd.' or 'Inc.' if an English trade name is concurrently registered. For foreign investors, the English name is phonetically transliterated into Hangul; alternatively, a uniquely devised Hangul name may be used, but it must not be identical or confusingly similar to any previously registered name. Foreign-language characters are not permitted in the statutory name field.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the IRO rejects the proposed name, the applicant must, within seven calendar days of receipt of the electronic rejection notice, submit a written objection to the Commercial Registration Division of the relevant district court. The objection must specify the exact rejected name, the acceptance number assigned by the IRO, a copy of the rejection notice, and a legal memorandum explaining compliance with Articles 18 to 22 of the Commercial Act. The court must decide within five business days. If the objection is dismissed, the applicant has two weeks to file an immediate appeal under the Non-Litigation Case Procedure Act to the appellate review chamber. During both stages, the applicant may simultaneously reserve and file an alternative name to avoid operational delay. No filing fee is required for the initial objection, but a KRW 5,000 court stamp for the appeal is paid to the court cashier.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office composed only of a mailing address, a call-forwarding service, and no physical staff or dedicated lease in the company's name will be rejected by the Korean National Tax Service when applying for the business registration certificate (saeopja deungrok), and Korean commercial banks will refuse to open a corporate current account. For the low-code website builder business, the tax agency requires a physical place of business with a lease contract, a visible company nameplate, and the possibility of on-site presence during regular business hours. A premium serviced office with a dedicated desk, a meeting room, and a lease in the company's name is acceptable. Therefore, a pure virtual office is effectively impermissible; a serviced office is the minimum acceptable solution.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: (1) a company nameplate at the registered address; (2) a lease agreement in the name of the Chusik Hoesa; (3) utility bills matching the address; (4) availability of the corporate seal and a responsible person on site; (5) basic office equipment or server logs indicating actual operation. Quantified risk: low to moderate, approximately 25% during the first fiscal year for a low-risk online service business; rises to 45% if the company claims VAT refunds or undergoes a change-of-representative registration. Unannounced visits are performed by municipal tax inspectors and, less commonly, by the district court verification officer for the registered agent, under the Framework Act on National Taxes.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Supreme Court of the Republic of Korea (district court registry)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Court Fees Act fixed fee for stock company registration

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed Korean attorney or qualified corporate agent

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 1000, as amended ex officio; Korean title romanized as Sangbeop), particularly Articles 288, 289, 292, 295, 297, 300, 306, 310-312, 316, 317, and 318; Commercial Registration Act (Act No. 5057, as amended), particularly Articles 14, 17, and 29; and the Enforcement Decree of the Commercial Registration Act.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Registration Office of the Local District Court having territorial jurisdiction over the registered office, administered by the Supreme Court of Korea through the National Court Administration.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Stock Company, together with the notarized Articles of Incorporation and the incorporation report submitted under Article 317 of the Commercial Act.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is required for a Chusik Hoesa under the Commercial Act after the 2012 amendment. However, the promoters and subscribers must pay in full the aggregate issue price of all subscribed shares into a licensed bank account before the incorporation registration is filed, and the paid-in funds may not be withdrawn until the incorporation registration is lawfully completed. There is no separate government escrow account requirement beyond this statutory payment restriction.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTIONS OF THE FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [COMPANY NAME] INC. (CHUSIK HOESA). The Board of Directors of [Company Name] Inc., a Korean stock corporation duly incorporated under the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea, held its first meeting at the registered office on [Date] at [Time]. The representative director presented the certificate of incorporation registration, the share subscription register, the bank payment certificate, the notarized Articles of Incorporation, and the minutes of the statutory organizational meeting. A lawful quorum was present, and each director was given reasonable notice of the meeting. 1. SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION AND ISSUANCE. RESOLVED, that the Board ratifies and confirms the subscription and full payment of the paid-in capital of [Amount] Korean Won by the subscribers named in the share subscription register, which amount is represented by [Number] ordinary shares with a par value of [Par Value] Korean Won each. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the paid-in capital was wired or deposited into the Company's subscription bank account prior to incorporation registration and that no part of those funds was withdrawn before the issuance of the certificate of incorporation registration. The Board confirms that the share capital is fully paid and available for lawful corporate purposes and that the issuance of shares complied with Article 295 of the Commercial Act. The Board approves the form of share certificate and directs the representative director to issue and deliver each subscriber a share certificate promptly after registration. 2. BANKING AUTHORIZATION AND PAYMENT RAILS. RESOLVED, that the representative director and the chief financial officer are authorized, acting jointly for any disbursement above [Threshold] Korean Won and individually for ordinary receipts, to open, maintain, and operate demand deposit, settlement, payroll, foreign currency, and merchant settlement accounts with [Bank Name]. RESOLVED FURTHER, that such authorized persons may execute e-banking mandates, sign SWIFT instructions, configure Stripe Billing and Paddle as the Company's online payment processors, and sign all agreements and instruments necessary for payment acceptance, treasury management, and statutory tax payment. 3. REGISTERED OFFICE ADOPTION. RESOLVED, that the premises located at [Full Address] are adopted and approved as the Company's registered office and principal business office for statutory purposes. The representative director is directed to file the adoption of the registered office with the Commercial Registry Office, to display the Company name at that place, and to update the National Tax Service and all relevant counterparties of the registered address. 4. STATUTORY OFFICER APPOINTMENTS. RESOLVED, that [Director A] is appointed as Chief Executive Officer and Representative Director, [Director B] is appointed as Chief Financial Officer, and [Auditor Name] is appointed as statutory auditor for the first fiscal period. These appointments shall continue until the first ordinary general meeting of shareholders or until successors are lawfully elected. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the Chief Executive Officer is authorized to register the corporate seal, to file tax registrations, to engage counsel and accountants, to execute service agreements with Stripe and Paddle, and to perform all other acts necessary or incidental to the corporate governance and lawful operation of the Company. 5. RECORD AND AUTHENTICITY. RESOLVED, that the minutes of this meeting be transcribed in the corporate minute book and signed by the chairman and directors, and that the corporate secretary is directed to transmit certified extracts of these resolutions to banks, tax authorities, and payment partners as required. There being no further business, the meeting was duly adjourned. [Signature Block]

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name clearance, drafting, and notarization of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Online Commercial Registration System (I-Ro) of the National Court Administration; final name review by the Commercial Registration Office of the Local District Court; notarization by a Korean notary public
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Promoters must first verify the proposed corporate name through the online registration system to ensure that it is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing Korean company. The Articles of Incorporation must then be drafted in accordance with Article 289 of the Commercial Act, setting out the corporate name, the precise business purpose, the registered office address, the total number of authorized shares, the par value, the shares to be issued at incorporation, the method of public notice, the number of directors, and the duration of the company. The articles must be written in Korean and notarized by a Korean notary public; without notarization the registry will reject the later filing. The business purpose should expressly include software publishing, digital content production, visual website template services, low-code and no-code application building, e-commerce enablement, and all other information technology services permitted under Korean law. The promoters should also confirm that the intended registered office address is located within the territorial jurisdiction of the intended registry.
required_dossiers: Valid passport or resident identification of each promoter
Power of attorney for any representative promoter
Provisional corporate name clearance confirmation
Draft Articles of Incorporation
Lease contract or letter of intent for the registered office address
Notarization request form and notary fee payment evidence
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is unavailable or is refused by the registry, the promoters must select two alternative names and re-submit the name search. If the notary or the registry queries the Articles of Incorporation, the promoters must amend the articles by a supplemental notarial deed and re-submit. Any correction order from the Commercial Registration Office must be satisfied within the stated cure period, normally three to fourteen days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Full payment of subscription price and statutory organizational meeting
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Korean commercial bank designated as the subscription bank; promoters' statutory organizational meeting convened under Articles 295 and 297 of the Commercial Act
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the Articles of Incorporation are notarized, the promoters must open a restricted subscription account in the name of the company with a licensed Korean bank. Each subscriber must pay the full subscription price for each subscribed share by wire transfer or cash deposit, and the bank must issue a deposit certificate confirming the aggregate paid-in capital. The promoters then convene the statutory organizational meeting before incorporation registration. At the meeting the promoters must report the capital contribution, approve the incorporation plan, elect the initial directors and the statutory auditor, and adopt the procedures for transferring subscribed funds into the operational corporate bank account after registration. Minutes of the organizational meeting must be signed and kept with the subscription register. If a non-resident subscriber is involved, the remittance receipts and a foreign investment report under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act must be prepared before the registration filing. Cryptocurrency or convertible instrument payments are not acceptable for paid-in capital.
required_dossiers: Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Share subscription register
Bank-issued capital deposit certificate
Identity documents of all subscribers and promoters
Remittance receipts and foreign investment declaration, if any
Signed minutes of the statutory organizational meeting
Payment records showing full and timely funding
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If payment is short or late, the subscriber must make up the full amount before the organizational meeting can validly proceed. If the bank certificate is defective or omits the company name, the promoters must request an amended certificate. If a subscriber defaults, the promoters may exclude that subscriber and reallocate the defaulted shares to another person, followed by a revised payment certificate and updated subscription register.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of incorporation registration with the local district court registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Registration Office of the Local District Court with jurisdiction over the registered office; filing through the I-Ro online portal or the court counter
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Immediately after the statutory organizational meeting, the promoters or their duly authorized agent must file the application for incorporation registration in the prescribed form under the Commercial Registration Act. The application must attach the notarized Articles of Incorporation, the bank payment certificate, the minutes of the organizational meeting, the written acceptance of each director and auditor, the register of directors with resident identification numbers, proof of the registered office, and the Korean corporate seal report. The registry will verify the legality of the incorporation process, the adequacy of the business object, and the payment of capital. The applicant must pay the registration license tax, local education tax, and court filing fee at the current statutory rates; for a minimum capital company the aggregate court and registration charges are approximately KRW 78,000, converted in the official fee field as USD 58. Upon approval, the registry assigns a corporate registration number and the company comes into existence as a juridical person.
required_dossiers: Application for registration of incorporation of a stock company
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Bank deposit certificate for paid-in capital
Minutes of the statutory organizational meeting
Written acceptance of each director and statutory auditor
Lease agreement or owner consent for the registered office
Korean corporate seal report form
Power of attorney, if filed by a third-party agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a correction order, the applicant must supply the missing documents or cure the irregularity within the period fixed by the registry, normally three to fourteen days. If the registry refuses the registration, the applicant may file an immediate appeal under the Commercial Registration Act, or re-file after remedying the defective ground. Where rejection arises from an incomplete notarial certificate, a fresh notarization and re-payment of fees will be required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-registration governance, tax registration, bank activation, and digital licensing verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: District Tax Office under the National Tax Service; licensed commercial bank; Financial Services Commission and Ministry of Economy and Finance for foreign-exchange and foreign-investment reporting; Korea Industrial Complex Authority only for future factory activities
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receiving the certificate of incorporation registration and the corporate seal certificate, the representative director must apply to the competent District Tax Office for a business registration certificate within twenty days of business commencement. Because the business is ISIC 6201, a pure no-code website builder and software publishing service, no manufacturing operating license, no factory establishment approval, and no Environmental Impact Assessment are required. The company must nevertheless open a corporate settlement account in compliance with anti-money laundering customer due diligence, with the director's identity and corporate documents presented to the bank. The company must prepare its share certificates, maintain the shareholder register and corporate minute book, and file any foreign-investment report if non-resident persons hold shares. Employment insurance and occupational safety insurance registrations must also be completed if employees are hired. The only physical licensing requirement is standard office fire safety and general workplace safety compliance, neither of which is an industrial license.
required_dossiers: Certificate of incorporation registration
Corporate seal certificate
Business registration application form
CEO and representative director identification
Registered office lease contract and deposit receipts
Corporate bank account opening application and customer due diligence forms
Share certificate counterfoils and shareholder register
Foreign investment report receipt, if non-resident ownership exists
Business scope description confirming ISIC 6201 no-code website builder activity
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the District Tax Office queries the classification, the applicant must submit a corrected business description showing the primary activity as software publishing and website template services under Korean Standard Industrial Classification 6201. If the bank refuses account opening because of authentication or beneficial ownership clarity, the company should cure the deficiency by providing a full corporate registry extract, then reapply. Any foreign-investment filing issue must be cured before transferring subscription proceeds out of the restricted account.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable. ISIC 6201 is a digital no-code software and website template service. No factory registration under the Industrial Cluster Development and Factory Establishment Act is triggered, and the Korea Industrial Complex Authority and municipal industrial licensing window are not involved for the formation of this entity.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable. No separate operating or manufacturing license is required. Only a National Tax Service Business Registration Certificate, issued under the Framework Act on National Taxes, is required for VAT, corporate income tax, and payroll withholding purposes.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable. For reference, the Ministry of Environment and the Korea Environment Corporation are the competent bodies only if a physical facility threshold is crossed; no such threshold exists for an ISIC 6201 digital software company.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable. The activity falls outside the mandatory EIA categories of the Environmental Impact Assessment Act. No full EIA, preliminary EIA, or environmental registration is required for a no-code website builder operating in an ordinary office.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable. There are no industrial process wastewater discharges, VOC emission points, or hazardous waste generation from software development and template publishing. Office wastewater is connected through the municipal sewer and is subject only to ordinary building-level domestic sewage standards. If the company later adds warehousing or fulfillment operations, it must re-evaluate waste registration and discharge permitting at that time.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable for a Civil Defense industrial fire permit. The digital enterprise must still comply with the Fire Safety Management Act for leased office premises, including fire extinguishers, evacuation routes, and fire-fighting equipment, and with the Occupational Safety and Health Act for general workplace accident prevention. No manufacturing-specific civil defense clearance is required because ISIC 6201 has no fire-loaded industrial plant or chemical storage.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) through the HomeTax electronic tax portal (hometax.go.kr), with export customs verification through the Korea Customs Service (KCS) UNI-PASS system (unipass.customs.go.kr).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign non-resident entity intending to supply taxable goods or services in South Korea must appoint a Korean tax representative and execute a power of attorney in HomeTax using the NTS tax-representative management function. The representative files an Application for Business Registration (Sa-eopja-deungrok-shincheongseo) with the competent district NTS office, attaching evidence of foreign incorporation, constitutional documents and board resolution appointing the local agent, proof of Korean business site or agent location, and, for electronic service suppliers, a simplified registration declaration as a foreign electronic service provider. Chusik Hoesa corporations formed in Korea apply within 20 days from business commencement. NTS issues the unified Korean Business Registration Number (BRN), a 10-digit identifier formatted 000-00-00000, used simultaneously for corporate income tax withholding, employment and indirect tax obligations, and VAT registration. For foreign non-resident suppliers of electronic services to Korean consumers, VAT registration through a tax representative is compulsory before or within 20 days after supply commencement, even in the absence of a domestic physical place of business.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. South Korea does not permit a US-style check-the-box pass-through election for a Chusik Hoesa. The entity is taxed on its income at the corporate level under the Corporate Tax Act. There is no hybrid-mismatch entity classification election available to change the default corporate status.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Value-Added Tax Act
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: KRW 0 - no monetary registration threshold is imposed for a domestic Chusik Hoesa or for a foreign non-resident supplier of electronic services. VAT registration is mandatory from the first taxable business activity. The simplified taxpayer regime is limited to small individual businesses and does not apply to incorporated entities. A foreign electronic service supplier must register through a tax representative irrespective of turnover, with no statutory de-minimis exemption for corporations.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Korea does not mandate real-time continuous clearance or digital stamping. Domestic suppliers subject to electronic tax invoicing must issue tax invoices through HomeTax e-tax-invoice or an NTS-certified EDI/API connection and transmit them to the NTS by the statutory due date, normally by the day following issuance. B2B supply is documented by a Korean tax invoice; B2C cash sales may be documented through the cash receipt system, and credit card sales slips serve as VAT vouchers. Foreign nonresident electronic service suppliers use the simplified NTS electronic-services return system and must retain transaction-level records, including customer identity and place of supply, while issuing a Korean e-tax invoice only for B2B purchasers that request one.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies under Article 21 of the Value-Added Tax Act to physically exported goods that are cleared through Korean Customs on UNI-PASS and to services exported to foreign customers where the place of supply is outside Korea, the service is used outside Korea, and payment is received in foreign currency. For a no-code website builder, cross-border digital platform services and web templates supplied to non-resident business customers qualify as zero-rated export services only if the supplier keeps contemporaneous evidence of the customer's offshore establishment, the non-Korean place of consumption, and foreign-currency receipt. Supplies made to Korean consumers or to Korean business customers for use in Korea are domestic supplies subject to 10% VAT.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Export Declaration approved by the Korea Customs Service on UNI-PASS
Commercial invoice and export/supply contract identifying the foreign purchaser and exact service/goods scope
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing departure of goods from Korea, where physical goods are involved
Packing list and export customs documentation matching the UNI-PASS declaration, where physical goods are involved
Foreign-exchange receipt certificate issued by a Korean foreign-exchange bank evidencing collection of export proceeds from the foreign buyer
Electronic zero-rated export tax invoice submitted through HomeTax
Service records proving offshore place of supply and foreign beneficial use for digital no-code builder and website-template exports
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The NTS and KCS jointly verify zero-rated export claims by cross-matching UNI-PASS declarations, tax invoices, shipping documents, and the exporter's foreign-exchange bank receipts. If documentation is absent, inconsistent, or proceeds are not repatriated within the required period, the zero rate is denied, the 10% VAT is recomputed and assessed, and statutory VAT additional tax for non-reporting, under-reporting or fraudulent reporting is imposed. Refunds already received are clawed back with interest-equivalent additional charges. Intentional false export declarations can trigger criminal sanctions under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act and referral to the Korea Customs Service for wrongdoing. The extended limitation period for fraudulent tax evasion and undeclared foreign exchange receipts is up to ten years.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK) and the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) acting jointly under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act (FETA); the BOK supervises designated foreign exchange banks and the MOEF issues foreign exchange policy, risk management guidelines, and capital account transaction regulations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Republic of Korea operates a heavily liberalized but regulated foreign exchange regime. Current account transactions such as service fees, royalties, and ordinary trade settlements are effectively fully convertible and require only a direct report to a designated foreign exchange bank, not prior approval. Capital account transactions, including foreign direct investment (FDI) into a Chusik Hoesa, are free but subject to mandatory notification and reporting under the FETA and the Foreign Investment Promotion Act (FIPA). Foreign capital can be freely injected via a Foreign Investment Capital Deposit Account, but the initial notification must be filed prior or contemporaneous with the deposit. Profit remittances, dividends, and proceeds from the sale of equity are permissible without conversion restrictions provided that the originating bank confirms the source funds and the tax status (i.e., dividend withholding under the Korea–foreign tax treaty). A significant hurdle is the requirement to provide a bank certificate of the inward remittance and a tax clearance certificate from the Korean tax office before repatriating large sums. Additionally, the KRW is not fully convertible outside Korea; offshore trading of the won is heavily curbed, and all physical or financial exchange of KRW must clear through a domestic authorized bank. Thus, the system is not an Article VIII hard-CAPEX surrender regime but rather a transparent current-account free, capital-account managed model with strict documentary trails.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the current FETA and the Foreign Exchange Transaction Guidance (directives 8-2 and 8-3), there is no mandatory surrender ratio for export foreign currency receipts. Exporters may retain foreign currency in a Foreign Currency Deposit Account at a designated foreign exchange bank. However, export proceeds must effectively be repatriated to Korea within the statutory settlement period, generally 6 months (180 days) from the date of the export declaration or the completion of the service, unless an extension is granted by the foreign exchange bank or the MOEF for justifiable trade credit reasons. Once repatriated, the exporter may choose to convert the receipts into KRW using market rates or hold them in foreign currency for future disbursements, subject to normal transaction reporting thresholds. For services rendered by a no-code website builder (ISIC 6201), the service export receipt must be settled through a Korean foreign exchange bank with a declaration under the appropriate service revenue code (e.g., 'Computer and Information Services' or 'Software Development Royalties'), and the bank will verify the underlying contract to classify the receipt as a current account item.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Foreign Investment Capital Deposit Account and Basic Operational KRW Currency Account
Multi-Currency Corporate Settlement Account (KRW Current Account plus Foreign Currency Deposit)
Trade Services and Corporate Liquidity Account with Export Proceeds Collection Facility
Capital Escrow / Foreign Investor KEB Hana Special Account and Daily Operational KRW Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore digital EMIs are not viable as a primary treasury or liquidity clearing venue for a Korean Chusik Hoesa. Under Korean banking law, only institutions designated as foreign exchange banks by the MOEF/BOK are permitted to provide foreign exchange settlement, KRW/FCY conversion, and cross-border remittance services. Payment facilitators such as Stripe and Paddle may be used as inbound sales collection agents for global SaaS subscriptions, but they must either obtain a domestic e-payment pre-approval (Form 1 under the Electronic Financial Transactions Act) or partner with a Korean PG and a licensed bank to settle KRW proceeds into the company's domestic account. In practice, an offshore EMI cannot open a local KRW-based corporate account on behalf of the Chusik Hoesa; it can only debit/credit the funds through an underlying correspondent arrangement with a Korean bank. Therefore, the feasible model is: Stripe/Paddle collect client card payments in foreign currencies, then remit the net settlement to the company's foreign currency account at a Korean bank, or, if configured for local card acquiring, they route via a licensed domestic acquire and deposit KRW. The treasury blueprint should treat EMIs as a payment rail, never as a bank account holder.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: South Korean banks, reinforced by FIU and FATF amendments, require physical in-branch verification for the opening of a corporate bank account where any foreign individual exercises control. A statutory director who is a foreign national must appear in person at a branch of the Korean bank to sign the account mandate, undergo a compliance interview, and present the original passport or a notarised copy after consular verification. Remote opening via video or a foreign notary is not generally accepted for the primary director of a newly incorporated foreign-invested company. As a limited alternative, if the foreign director designates a Korean-resident representative or a local attorney-in-fact under a notarised and apostilled power of attorney, that proxy may appear in-branch with the director; however, the bank compliance officer will usually reserve the right to request a real-time video call with the foreign director and will refuse the account if the beneficial owner cannot be affirmatively identified.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foreign UBO opacity and nominee director suspicion in a freshly incorporated Chusik Hoesa with no operating history and a minority foreign shareholder in a software entity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised and apostilled passports of all shareholders and directors; certificate of incorporation and articles of association; UBO declaration form with full ownership chain; if beneficial owners are corporate entities, certified corporate registry extracts for each layer plus a source of wealth statement (bankable assets or audited financial statements) for individuals injecting capital.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Initial inbound equity remittance into a Foreign Investment Capital Deposit Account for a no-code website builder, which banks treat as high-risk due to the absence of physical assets or inventory to justify the capital amount.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank reference letter from the remitting institution; the Foreign Investment Notification (capital introduction) certificate from the Ministry of Economy and Finance; a detailed capital usage budget (AWS/Azure hosting, API credits, marketing spend, operational runway); lease or subcontractor proof for an actual Korean registered office; and the signed Board of Directors resolution confirming the purpose of the capital raise.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Outbound cross-border payments to cloud service providers, freelancers, and overseas affiliates creating a mismatch with the declared 'no-code website builder' commercial model, triggering a red flag for potential royalty leakage or avoidable service export underinvoicing.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed vendor contracts or service-level agreements with Microsoft, Google, AWS, and payment gateways; annual information security / SOC2 / data processing agreements; detailed invoices with usage metrics; tax invoices and VAT certificates for each service; an organisational overhead graph demonstrating that the platform builds upon third-party subprocessors; and a notarised record of the internal payment approval workflow.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Rapid or unexpected settlement receipts from Stripe/Paddle in high-volume cards from mixed jurisdictions, particularly if the company's stated treasury is in a domestic Korean bank, creating uncertainty under the Korean 'Know Your Transaction' standards.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Payment gateway settlement reports matched to Stripe/Paddle dashboards; merchant sale ledger with customer list and jurisdiction split; samples of customer invoices and proof of digital delivery logs (site builder project counts); the company's current-quarter sales tax and VAT returns; and a comprehensive log of refunds and chargebacks, if any, plus an AML self-assessment prepared under the Korean Financial Action Task Force guidance.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For the Korean Chusik Hoesa, all inbound equity capital must be routed via a designated foreign exchange bank. The foreign investor opens a Foreign Investment Capital Deposit Account (실명외화예금) in the remitting bank pre-incorporation or within the statutory period after incorporation, remits the capital by SWIFT MT103 with the purpose code 'Direct Investment – Foreign Investment Capital' (typically under the BOK balance-of-payments category 'Direct Investment: Equity Capital'), and the bank creates a Foreign Investment Notification under the FIPA. After the capital deposit clears, the bank issues a certificate of the foreign investment capital deposit, the company registers the investment with MOEF/KOTRA (if required for prior notification), and the bank sweeps the funds into the entity's KRW or multi-currency operational account upon verification of the company's business registration certificate and the receipt of the board's capital allocation resolution. Capital verification is achieved through the certified bank supporting note, the corporate financial statement entry for share capital, and the stock ledger showing the issuance of shares against the remittance. For subsequent profit remittances, the same bank requires the audited (or tax-accepted) financial statements, the dividend declaration, and a tax certificate showing the withholding amount.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For a Korean software company, outbound disbursements for cloud fees, outsourced contractors, API licensing, advertising, and affiliate partner commissions are settled using SWIFT MT103 corporate wire transfers. The company must code each payment with the appropriate foreign exchange classification (e.g., 'Technical Service Fee', 'Computer Software Royalty Payment', or 'Advertising and Market Research') and provide underlying invoices to the Korean bank to avoid classification as a capital outflow. Trade settlements for physical or IP sales, if any, may use Commercial Letters of Credit (LC) for substantial tangible goods / hardware bundles, but a no-code website builder is almost entirely a service transaction, so documentary collections are not a standard clearing rail. The preferred treasury protocol is to run all outbound operational payments through a single clearing bank with documented standing instructions, automated FX conversion from KRW to the target currency at competitive daily rates, and a daily liquidity forecast to keep the KRW and FCY account balances under standard anti-capital-flight reporting thresholds.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright USD/KRW spot for ordinary business receipts and payments, executed through a designated foreign exchange bank and supported by an underlying invoice or contract.

FX Forward / Forward Exchange Contract (FEC) with a maturity up to 12 months covering verified export collectibles or import payables, governed by the Foreign Exchange Transaction Guidance (Article 11).

Cross Currency Swap (CCS) used only to hedge medium/long-term foreign currency borrowings or foreign direct investment notes, requiring prior declaration to the bank and the existence of an actual credit or equity exposure.

Non-Deliverable Forward (NDF) in KRW is prohibited for domestic residents and for offshore speculative activity under Korean capital controls; if the treasury needs an NDF, it can only be transacted through a licensed international broker under a specific regulatory exemption for non-residents or for trade-related hedge purposes on an exceptional basis, and that route is not mutually recommended in a standard onboarding blueprint.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return and payment (Corporate Tax Act, article 60, 61)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after the fiscal year end; for calendar-year Chusik Hoesa, filing and payment due by 31 March
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file by deadline: 20% surtax on the unpaid tax base for non-filing; understatement surtax of 10% (20% for aggressive understatement or 40% for reckless/false declarations); late payment delinquency charge of 3% of unpaid tax for the initial month plus 1.2% per complete month thereafter; chronic non-payment triggers NTS tax collection measures, asset seizure, business registration closure, and possible court-ordered dissolution

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local corporate income tax return and payment (Local Tax Act)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local government tax office of the registered office (Municipal or Provincial administration)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed together with the national corporate income tax return; due within 3 months after the fiscal year end, with 31 March statutory deadline for calendar-year entities
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing surcharge of 10% of the payable local tax; unpaid local tax interest of 0.022% per day or equivalent local surcharges; forced collection including bank attachment and auction of corporate assets, and eventual administrative business closure

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual general meeting of shareholders and approval of annual financial statements (Commercial Act, article 365)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporate records (shareholders' meeting minutes maintained at registered office; no government filing is required solely for holding the AGM)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual shareholders' meeting must be convened within 3 months after the close of the fiscal year; for calendar-year companies, no later than 31 March
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: If the AGM is not held within the statutory period, each responsible director is subject to an administrative fine of up to KRW 5 million under Commercial Act article 635; failure may also invalidate management discharge, trigger shareholder derivative actions, and impair the company's ability to obtain or renew working capital from payment providers and banks

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Filing of approved balance sheet and attached financial documents with the registry court (Commercial Act, article 451)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local District Court Registration Office (registry court) in the jurisdiction of the registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 2 weeks after the shareholders' meeting approves the financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors who fail to file without just cause are subject to an administrative fine up to KRW 5 million; repeated failure to file over consecutive business years may be treated as an indicator of dormant status and can contribute to administrative strike-off through court dunning procedures and public notice

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statutory external audit report filing with the Financial Supervisory Service through DART (Act on External Audit of Stock Companies)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) - DART electronic disclosure system for the statutory external audit report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For companies subject to mandatory external audit, the auditor's report must be completed in time to accompany the corporate tax return; the audit report or a reference confirming its filing is submitted to FSS/DART within 2 weeks after the shareholders' meeting (for calendar-year companies, generally no later than 31 March for the audited financial statements attached to the annual tax return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or non-filing triggers penalties under the External Audit Act, including an administrative fine of up to KRW 10 million and public disclosure of non-compliance; the company's audit opinion may be noted as adverse or disclaimed, and the entity may be barred from specified licensing, financing, and public procurement; persistent non-compliance may lead to FSS referral to the enforcement committee and tax authorities for audit adjustment

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of business operation status and payment rail renewals via registered office / agent KYC refresh
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registered office provider and banking / payment partners (Stripe Billing / Paddle) as part of anti-money laundering and foreign account maintenance; no direct Korean government filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually upon the incorporation anniversary; for payment rails, within 30 days of any shareholding or beneficial ownership change to maintain KYC integrity
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain updated corporate KYC documentation can result in freezing or termination of merchant processing accounts and bank account restrictions; if accompanied by non-filing of tax returns, the NTS may suspend the business registration certificate, with escalation to administrative strike-off

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies and its Enforcement Decree, a Chusik Hoesa is mandatorily subject to an independent audit by a certified public accountant registered in Korea when total assets at the end of the preceding fiscal year reach or exceed KRW 12 billion (approximately USD 9.2 million); because the entity may also be caught by the small-company audit regime, a company with total assets of KRW 1 billion or more but below KRW 12 billion must undergo a statutory external audit (often a less extensive small-company audit) unless specifically exempted by law or FSS rules; additionally, a company is always required to be audited if it is a listed issuer, a public-interest company, a large business group affiliate, or is subject to FSS designation under the external audit rules. No revenue or headcount threshold alone triggers the audit, but if a company prepares consolidated or unconsolidated financial statements under applicable standards, the statutory audit covers those statements.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Public-interest companies and larger unlisted companies must apply Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS) as endorsed by the Korea Accounting Standards Board; smaller non-listed companies may apply Korean GAAP for small and medium entities (SME K-GAAP); all statutory audits must be conducted in accordance with Korean Standards on Auditing (KSA), which are aligned with ISAs; the audited financial statements must be approved at the annual shareholders' meeting and filed with the registry court and corporate tax authorities as applicable.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: South Korea does not maintain a public beneficial ownership register for a private Chusik Hoesa, and there is no annual UBO filing in the strict sense. However, the company must continuously maintain an accurate register of members and identify beneficial owners for bank and payment-service KYC purposes under the Financial Transaction Reports Act and the Real Name Financial Transaction and Confidentiality Act. A share transfer is effective between the parties upon delivery of share certificates, but the transferee may not assert shareholder rights against the company until the transfer is recorded in the company's register of members; the company must update the register upon written request. Where foreign residents acquire or transfer shares, a foreign exchange report must be made within 30 days of closing. For internal corporate governance, the company should reconfirm beneficial ownership at each annual general meeting and whenever a shareholder transfers more than a negligible interest to ensure payment rails, bank accounts, and the corporate registry reflect current ultimate owners.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Auditors (if any auditor is elected)
Register of Secured Bonds or Charges, if corporate bonds or secured loans are issued
Minute Book of general shareholders' meetings
Minute Book of board of directors' meetings

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 200 - 700 per annum for a registered office address and local corporate compliance agent retainer; USD 700 - 1,500 if certified bookkeeping support is included
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 8,000 - 25,000 for a mandatory statutory external audit of a small-to-mid-size Chusik Hoesa; if the entity falls below audit thresholds, a review or certified compilation of financial statements typically costs USD 3,000 - 8,000

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.2% combined top effective headline rate (22% national Corporate Tax Act rate on taxable income exceeding KRW 20 billion plus the mandatory 10% local income tax surcharge on the national corporate tax; lower brackets: 10% on taxable income up to KRW 200 million and 20% on taxable income between KRW 200 million and KRW 20 billion).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Qualifying foreign-invested enterprises under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act may enjoy corporate income tax exemption of 100% for the first five years and a 50% reduction for the following two years in Free Economic Zones and Foreign Investment Zones; qualifying R&D expenditure, including software and no-code platform development, may be eligible for R&D tax credits under the Special Tax Treatment Control Act; technology transfer income may qualify for income tax exemption; foreign-source dividend income may be exempt in whole or in part under domestic participation and anti-over-taxation rules for qualified Korean holding companies.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Tax Return and the annexed Corporate Tax Base and Tax Payable Calculation Statement filed through the National Tax Service HomeTax electronic filing system (hometax.go.kr) under the Enforcement Rules of the Corporate Tax Act.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; a mid-year estimated corporate tax payment is also required each fiscal year for corporations expecting taxable income.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual corporate income tax return must be filed within 3 months from the end of the relevant fiscal year; for a December 31 fiscal year-end, the statutory filing deadline is March 31 of the following year (or the next business day if the deadline falls on a holiday).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Identification of the filing corporate taxpayer: corporation name, unique business registration number, fiscal year start and end, industry code, head office address, and representative director details.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a Korean Chusik Hoesa ultimately held by non-resident shareholders, identify every direct foreign shareholder and state their jurisdiction of tax residence. Where treaty-reduced withholding rates are claimed on dividend distributions, attach the Tax Residency Certificates and beneficial ownership declarations before the return is filed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net income (loss) per financial statements prepared under Korean International Financial Reporting Standards or generally accepted accounting principles, before corporate tax adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A Korean resident Chusik Hoesa is taxed on worldwide income; do not exclude foreign revenue of the no-code website builder merely because the customer is overseas. A foreign corporation that is itself a taxpayer with a Korean permanent establishment would include only income effectively connected with the Korean PE.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax adjustments comprehensively schedule: disallowed expenses, non-deductible gifts and entertainment, cash expenditures, provisions, reserves, depreciation differences, and transfer pricing adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Payments to offshore related parties for fees, royalties, management charges, or no-code technology licensing must be tested against the arm's length standard under the Law for Coordination of International Tax Affairs. Expenses lacking supporting contracts, actual services, invoice trails, and Korean economic substance will be disallowed and reclassified.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Loss carryforward deduction: the portion of prior-year losses, incurred within the statutory carryforward period, that is available to be deducted in the current tax base.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only losses of the Korean tax resident entity computed under the Corporate Tax Act may be carried forward. Losses of a non-resident parent, a related foreign service company, or an intermediary IP-holding entity may not be pooled with or transferred to the Korean taxpayer.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable base after exemptions and deductions, the application of the progressive national corporate income tax rates, and the calculation of the national corporate income tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The entire income of the Korean Chusik Hoesa is subject to Korean progressive corporate rates irrespective of non-resident shareholding. No foreign participation exemption in the CIT return may be applied unless the precise Korean domestic statutory and treaty conditions are satisfied; cross-border low-code licensing revenue cannot be shifted to a shell entity without CIGA in the foreign jurisdiction.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Local income tax surcharge: calculation of the mandatory local income tax surcharge, equal to 10% of the national corporate income tax payable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The local income tax surcharge applies in all cases where national corporate tax is payable, including where the Korean entity is controlled by non-residents. It is not a separate branch profits tax and no treaty relief is ordinarily available against the local surcharge unless expressly protected by a comprehensive treaty.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign tax credit, withholding tax credit, and other tax incentive credits that reduce the final corporate income tax liability.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the Korean company itself received foreign-source dividends, interest, or royalties on which foreign withholding tax was suffered, attach official evidence and compute the Korean foreign tax credit carefully within the Corporate Tax Act. A Korean company cannot credit taxes that were economically borne by a non-resident shareholder or foreign related corporation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Summary of tax payable, amounts already paid by way of interim estimated and withholding payments, additional penalties, and net final tax due or refund claimed.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Where treaty-reduced withholding rates were not applied at source on profit repatriation or outbound royalty/interest payments, file a corrected return or a refund claim within the statutory period and attach all DTA substantiation, including the payer payment vouchers, withholding statements, and Tax Residency Certificate.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file the annual corporate tax return by the statutory deadline triggers an additional tax of 20% on the unpaid corporate tax (10% where no tax would have been due) plus daily interest surcharges for unreported or under-reported tax. Filing a false return or evading tax beyond the thresholds in the Korean Punishment for Tax Evasion Act may result in additional taxes of up to 40%, criminal investigation, fines, and imprisonment.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22% gross on outbound dividends paid to non-resident corporate shareholders: 20% national corporate withholding tax under the Corporate Tax Act plus the 10% local income tax surcharge producing a 2% local withholding component.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a bilateral Double Tax Treaty reduced dividend rate, the non-resident shareholder must submit to the Korean payor a current Tax Residency Certificate issued by the foreign tax authority, a completing beneficial ownership declaration, corporate register evidence, shareholding history, and a written application for reduced treaty withholding prior to payment. If the reduced rate was not applied at source, the non-resident must file a refund application with the National Tax Service attaching the withholding certificates, payment vouchers, TRC, and substantive evidence that the recipient, not a conduit back-to-back arrangement, is the true owner of the dividend flows.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: The statutory gross withholding rates for outbound interest and royalties are likewise 22% (20% national withholding tax plus 2% local surcharge). Treaties commonly reduce interest and royalty withholding rates to 10% or 15%, but only if the recipient is the beneficial owner and fully satisfies Korean treaty application and substance requirements.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: KRW 5,000,000,000 (5 billion Korean Won) of aggregate cross-border intercompany transactions with foreign related parties in a fiscal year triggers mandatory contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation, submission of the international related-party transaction report, and preparation of the Local File; Master File preparation must also be assessed against the global group revenue thresholds under the Law for Coordination of International Tax Affairs.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korea applies the substance-over-form doctrine and the anti-abuse and beneficial ownership standards under the Corporate Tax Act and the Law for Coordination of International Tax Affairs. A Korean entity is not automatically subject to Caribbean-style Economic Substance Regulations, but any Core Income-Generating Activities, strategic decision-making, personnel, physical presence, financial risk, and intangible development, enhancement, maintenance, protection, and exploitation functions must be adequately performed in the jurisdiction claiming the income; shell structures inserted solely to obtain treaty benefits or to dilute Korean taxable profit will be recharacterized or disregarded.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion and Fraudulent Corporate Tax Filing
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately understating Korean-source revenue of the Chusik Hoesa no-code website builder, fabricating deductions, inflating expenses, or shifting web template and low-code platform revenue to an offshore entity without real operations or arm's length pricing.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Assessment of additional national corporate income tax, local income tax, interest surcharges, and a negligence penalty of up to 40% of the under-reported tax; criminal sanction under the Korean Punishment for Tax Evasion Act and the Act on the Aggravated Punishment of Specific Crimes includes imprisonment for up to 3 years or, for aggravated evasion above statutory thresholds, up to 7 years and substantial criminal fines.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign or cause false corporate tax returns may have the corporate veil pierced under the illegal transaction and gross negligence doctrines; personal assets are subject to civil restitution and attachment, the National Tax Service may impose a travel ban and immigration exit restriction, and directors face criminal imprisonment and disqualification from serving on future corporate boards.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Documentation Failure and Non-Arm's Length Intercompany Pricing
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to prepare, retain, or submit the required contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation and the international related-party transaction report while paying excessive royalties, management fees, or commissions to a foreign related corporation for no-code platform technology or customer acquisition support, without a functional and risk analysis.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The National Tax Service may make a transfer pricing adjustment under the Law for Coordination of International Tax Affairs, increasing the Korean taxable income to arm's length levels, imposing corrected tax and interest, and applying statutory documentation penalties and negligence penalties; foreign transaction reporting failures carry separate monetary fines per form.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly execute or backdate false intercompany agreements are jointly and severally liable for the resulting corporate tax deficiency; personal bank accounts and property can be seized, the directors may be blacklisted as chronic delinquent taxpayers and prevented from leaving Korea, and criminal liability may be prosecuted under the transfer pricing anti-evasion provisions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company Structure, Treaty Shopping, and Abusive DTA Withholding Claims
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using a tax-treaty intermediate shell corporation without staff, premises, substantial board activity, or economic substance in the claimed jurisdiction solely to obtain a reduced withholding tax rate on Korean-sourced dividends, interest, or royalties, or to receive Korean profits without Korean economic substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty benefits on the basis that the recipient is not the beneficial owner, reclassification of the income as fully Korean-source income, reassessment of withholding tax at the statutory 22% rate, imposition of additional taxes of up to 20% of unreported withheld amounts, and monetary penalties for failure to satisfy treaty application requirements.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and ultimate controllers of the Korean paying entity are personally liable for aiding an abusive DTA claim; authorities may disregard the intermediary entity, attach the Korean company's assets, place the directors on immigration watchlists, and pursue criminal charges for deceptive documentation and tax evasion, with imprisonment terms and clawback of the distributed or royalty income through civil asset recovery.
